_what_this_is: Branch B task configuration for the OPENMM route: how one (basin, seed)
quasi-harmonic trajectory is placed on a machine when it is produced by
scripts/production/s0_B_qha_trajectory_openmm.py rather than by the ASE driver.
The SCIENCE settings are NOT here. The timestep, the coupling time, the temperature,
the sampling interval and the three prohibitions live in the driver and in
configs/mdp/s0_qha_production.mdp; the standard state lives in configs/openqha.yaml.
Choosing a machine must never change a result -- that is the whole point of branch E.
If a value appears both here and in one of those files, that file wins and this one
Read hpc/configs/qha_md.json first. Everything there applies unless contradicted
below, and most of it is not contradicted: the granularity, the CPU ruling, the
one-thread ruling, the walltime policy and the failure policy are the same because
they are properties of the WORK, not of the library that does it.

_why: This route does not run in the same environment as the other one, and that is not
an accident to be tidied away. `openqha` has ASE and MACE 0.3.16; `qm9fe` has
OpenMM, openmm-torch, openmmtools and mdtraj. openmm-torch has to match the
pytorch build it was compiled against, and putting both stacks in one environment
is the same class of hazard as two BLAS providers -- which this repository already
spent a measurement on (see environment.yml).
So the executor for this task class must launch a DIFFERENT interpreter. A resource
config that ignores this will run the ASE stack and produce trajectories that are
not what this file describes.

thermostat._status: openmmtools' OWN documented defaults, adopted rather than chosen
_why: The coupling time is the whole decision and it is measured, not preferred. On a
harmonic surface built from the production potential's own Hessian, where the
answer is known in closed form, a 100 fs coupling returns the softest mode at 179
cm^-1 against a true 79.7 and costs 1.15 kcal/mol on T*S; 419 fs -- the intuitive
choice, matched to that mode's period -- costs 1.23. The KINETIC temperature is
correct in every one of those runs, so nothing about them looks wrong.
50 ps^-1 is openmmtools' default AND the value in the QHA reference paper this
branch cites (rinaldo2003). openqha.qha.assert_trajectory_identity refuses a
coupling time above 20 fs and a chain shorter than 3, so this is enforced rather
than documented.
A fallback to openmm.NoseHooverIntegrator exists if openmmtools is missing. It is
NOT the same propagator -- 7-term Yoshida-Suzuki rather than 5 -- and the driver
records which one ran in every product rather than treating them as equivalent.
No neighbour search at all. Branch B's molecules have 10 to 19 atoms, so the exact
neighbour list IS the complete graph, and pairs beyond r_max contribute exactly
zero because MACE's radial cutoff function is exactly zero there -- measured
bit-identical with half the edges outside the cutoff.
Two consequences worth stating. The graph is STATIC, which is what makes
torch.jit.trace sound (torch.jit.script FAILS: e3nn 0.4.4 is not scriptable). And
there is no box to anchor, so this route cannot have the origin-anchoring defect
that openqha/mace_patch.py guards the other route against -- which matters here
because in the qm9fe environment `import mace` resolves to the vendored develop
tree, which HAS that defect.
NNPOps and openmm-ml are deliberately not dependencies.

verified_against_ase._status: checked at the start of EVERY run; the driver refuses to continue if it fails

_device_why: CPU, for the same reason as the ASE route: a thermostatted trajectory is a serial
chain of single-structure force calls, which is the case D0-56 measured as not
filling a card. OpenMM's CUDA platform does not change that -- the cost is in the
MACE forward pass inside a TorchForce, not in the integration.
OpenMM's platform name is passed separately (--platform) because 'Reference' is
useful for debugging and is 10x slower; CPU is the production choice.
_memory_why: 4 GB rather than the ASE route's 3: this process holds an OpenMM context, a torch
model AND its traced copy. Measured RSS on acetone was well under that; the margin
is for the 19-atom species, which has not been measured.

cost_measured._status: MEASURED 2026-09-04 on this machine, acetone (10 atoms), 1 thread, CPU platform
_warning: The ASE route measured 96.1 s/ps uncontended on the same molecule. These two
numbers are close enough to plan with and NOT close enough to call equal: the
OpenMM figure was taken on a loaded machine, and neither has been measured with
many concurrent trajectories on one node. Do not divide either by a worker count
The production length is set by the saturation curve, not chosen in advance. At 25
ps acceptance criterion 1 FAILED (+0.4684 kcal/mol over the last doubling, budget
0.3), so the real per-task cost is larger than any figure here implies.

_why: Same policy as the ASE route, but note a difference that matters for pre-emption:
this driver flushes frames.npy every CHUNK_FRAMES samples and can resume from
them, but it does NOT yet checkpoint the Nose-Hoover chain's extended-system
variables. A resumed task therefore restarts the thermostat's internal state.
That is recorded here rather than hidden because it is a real limitation: the
frames are still a valid canonical sample, but a resumed trajectory is not
bit-identical to an uninterrupted one, which the ASE route's state.npz does
achieve. Prefer a walltime that fits a whole trajectory on this route.
As the ASE route. A trajectory that falls apart will fall apart again from the same
basin with the same seed, and there is no fallback of any kind: the driver refuses
to start if its force does not reproduce the ASE calculator, and
qha.assert_trajectory_identity refuses the product if the coupling time or chain
length is outside what was calibrated.

_note: Placement must not change a number. The scientific criteria are plan_B's and
scripts/production/s0_B_qha_analyse.py tests all of them; the criteria here are
about the trajectories meaning the same thing wherever they ran.
Cross-machine bit-reproducibility is NOT demanded, for the reason given in
qha_md.json: molecular dynamics is chaotic and a last-bit difference in one force
call separates two trajectories exponentially. Measured on this repository: a rigid
1e-14 A shift -- an exact symmetry of the potential -- grew to 2.5e-11 A over 3 ps,
an e-folding time of about 0.4 ps.
acceptance.force_matches_ase: openqha.openmm_mace.verify_against_ase agrees in energy to 1e-9 eV and in forces to 1e-6 eV/A, checked at the start of every run
acceptance.same_machine_same_seed: a (basin, seed) rerun uninterrupted on the same machine reproduces frames.npy byte for byte
acceptance.cross_machine: T*S_QH from the same (basin, seed) on another machine must agree within the seed-to-seed noise floor that acceptance criterion 5 measures
acceptance.route_agreement: T*S_QH from this route and from the ASE route, at the same length and species, must agree within that same noise floor -- this is the check the two-route design exists for
acceptance.identity_assertion: every trajectory's metadata passes qha.assert_trajectory_identity, including the Nose-Hoover coupling time and chain length
